story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price DIVISLAB to move about ±6.6%, roughly 10,824 to 12,366. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 65% of the time.
DIVISLAB has actually been moving about 2.26% a day this past month: very high for it against the past year.

For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 12,000 (+3.8% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 11,000 (-4.8%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
Options are cheap compared with how much DIVISLAB has actually been moving: they price 28.3% a year while the last month realised 35.8%.

Since 2019-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 69% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal +0.21 vol pts (front month), 63rd percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.53; all-expiry OI PCR at the 5th percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +120,300, puts +54,300 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.analyst: Near-month basis +29.5, annualised carry 2.9% (13th percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 5.9%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Short build-up, Long build-up, Long build-up, Long unwinding, Long unwinding. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 6.65% (forward 11,595.3). Scored on 1,935 days since 2019-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.
